incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — GPU memory collapse detected in us-west-2 serving pool (service: runtime-prefill). Auto-page to oncall (lee_oncall).
lee_oncall: On call — looking. Any customer-facing failures yet?
maria_runtime: Seeing continuous OOMKilled on a subset of prefill containers. Long sequences (~>1.2M tokens across prefix) pushing vram.
raj_sre: Node  ip-10-0-5-42 flapped (kube reports container OOMKilled, restart_count=3). dmesg snapshot shows `Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (python)`.
lee_oncall: Pushing logs from the affected pod:```
2026-03-18T02:12:01Z runtime[pid=2345]: CUDA out of memory when allocating 12.3GiB
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/infer.py\", line 412, in prefill
    kv_store.alloc(... )
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```
alice_ops: Rolling a quick mitigation: temporarily stop routing 3 heavy-model variants to the hot pool, route to encoded-quantized fallback instances. Applying now.
maria_runtime: Suggest immediate soft-limits: cap prefill_seq_len to 512k tokens for affected route, enable prefix trim for requests >200k, and trigger kvcache aggressive-evict. Will prepare a rollout.
raj_sre: Scaling up ephemeral nodes isn't helpful — same request footprint will kill more GPUs. We should shed heavy requests instead of scaling. Recommend throttling large-context requests to queued slowpath.
kristen_support: Support — customers reporting increased 502s for long document uploads in US-WEST-2. Current affected customer fraction estimated ~3.8%. Need status update for customer comms.
lee_oncall: Applying route change now (via deploy-bot).`deploy-bot: routing-update apply --region us-west-2 --route /v1/chat?model=large-long -> fallback-quantized --reason \"oom mitigation\"`
deploy-bot: Applied routing update to 42 instances.
maria_runtime: Enabling kvcache trim policy and reducing max_prefill_window to 4096 tokens for the heavy endpoints. Patch ID: runtime/patch/5890001.
raj_sre: Observability: token-rate dropped for heavy requests, memory pressure easing. Node restarts reduced to 0 in the last 4m.
lee_oncall: Customer impact baseline: 502 spike started 02:11Z, mitigated 02:17Z. Peak error rate for heavy-ctx route ~12% locally, overall weighted ~3.8%. Noting for postmortem.
kristen_support: Drafting customer note: "We experienced increased errors for very large-context requests in US-WEST-2 between 02:11-02:17Z. We applied routing and trimming mitigations; net effect: reduced errors and degraded to fallback models for a small subset. Follow-up from eng w/ root cause soon."
alice_ops: Temporary guardrails in place: 1) hard cap 512k tokens on allowed prefill length in the gateway 2) route >200k to queued slowpath 3) enable fallback-quantized. Will revert only after stability window.
maria_runtime: Recommend follow-up actions: reproduce with synthetic large-seq job, add server-side request-size histogram alert at 95th/99th, add automated prefill memory prediction to reject-before-schedule.
raj_sre: Creating an incident ticket and assigning a postmortem to @maria_runtime and @lee_oncall. Ticket: INC-5890.
lee_oncall: Monitoring for 30m. Will hand off to daytime rotation at 02:47Z if stable. :white_check_mark:
kristen_support: Notifying impacted customers now (template sent).
incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated -> monitoring. Severity remains P1 until postmortem published.
lee_oncall: Thanks team. If memory pressure resurfaces, we'll escalate to full bridge. For now, keep traces for 90d and show the eval prompts that triggered the largest prefill sizes. :ear:
